title: Higher open direct images over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic different from $\ell$,
let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $F$ be a constructible
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. Then $Rj_*F\in D^b_c(Y,\mathbf F_\ell)$.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

proof.text: Set $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with its identity structure morphism over $k$. A field has exactly one prime ideal, $(0)$, and no nonzero nilpotents, so $S$ is integral and its underlying space is a singleton. Its identity morphism is of finite type: $k$ is generated over itself by the empty set. The given $X,Y$ are finite-type $S$-schemes, $j$ is an open immersion, and $F$ is constructible on $X$ with coefficients $\mathbf F_\ell$, where $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$. Thus all hypotheses of [thm-fin-deligne-generic-open] hold.

Apply [thm-fin-deligne-generic-open] to these data. It gives a nonempty open $U\subset S$ for which $Rj_{U,*}(F|_{X_U})\in D^b_c(Y_U,\mathbf F_\ell)$. Since $S$ has one point, $U=S$ as an open subscheme. Consequently $X_U=X$, $Y_U=Y$, $j_U=j$, and $F|_{X_U}=F$ under the canonical identity identifications. Substituting these equalities gives $Rj_*F\in D^b_c(Y,\mathbf F_\ell)$ in the ordinary derived category, exactly the claimed boundedness and constructibility. The additional exchange-isomorphism conclusion of the cited theorem is not used.

proof.text:
Apply [thm-fin-deligne-generic-open] with
$S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its only nonempty open is $S$
itself, so the generic conclusion is the assertion on all of $Y$.
No stratification of $Y$ and no closed-base-change assertion
for $Rj_*$ is needed here.
